title: Secondary control-plane subnet handoff, transient peering cleanup, and DNS fallback for rolling upgrades
author: Anika Patel
description: Motivation: rolling control-plane upgrades for Private deployments require a safe handoff path between control-plane subnets in multi-AZ clusters. Existing flows rely on long-lived VPC peering and manual cleanup which blocks fast upgrades and causes transient routing conflicts. This PR implements an automated secondary control-plane subnet handoff, transient peering that exists only for the duration of the upgrade, and a DNS fallback and TTL tuning strategy to avoid flip-flop during CANARY and blue/green rollouts. Design summary: 1) Terraform module changes add a secondary_controlplane_subnet resource set and a transient_peering module that creates one-off peering attachments with explicit lifecycle rules. 2) The installer orchestration (helm + upgrade controller) now performs a 4-step handoff: provision secondary subnet, create transient peering with limited route propagation, migrate control-plane ENIs via the installer-hooks, perform DNS TTL reduction and swap, then gracefully remove peering and secondary subnet. 3) Security posture: segregated security groups for handoff traffic, temporary SG rules with expiration tags, and validation hooks that enforce least-privilege egress during the transient window. 4) Rollback: installer records an idempotent reversal path that recreates previous DNS records, re-establishes previous peering if needed, and reconciles route tables. Implementation notes: Terraform 1.5-compatible module added under terraform/modules/controlplane-handoff with parameterized az_affinity, peering_ttl_minutes and cleanup_grace_seconds. Helm chart changes include an upgrade-controller chart hook that calls a new job template upgrade-hook-controlplane-handoff.yaml; values.yaml exposes handoff.enabled, handoff.dns_ttl_seconds and handoff.fail_open (default false). The installer CLI gains a new flag --handoff-dry-run that performs full preflight and simulates peering lifecycle without committing. Verification: added unit tests for module plan diffs and integration tests in perf-canary that run a simulated 3-AZ upgrade path with synthetic load and assert no >200ms spike in control-plane RPC latencies. Security review: performed static IAM policy scan and added automated tag-based cleanup guardrails. Migration and rollout guidance: incremental rollout recommended behind the existing canary gate; reduce DNS TTL to 30s before handoff; monitor control-plane latency and kubelet heartbeats. Backout steps are documented in release_notes and installer runbook. Risks and mitigations: risk of route table race during peering create is mitigated by sequenced route propagation and a preflight route conflict detector that pauses handoff and alerts. The PR does not change defaults; handoff.enabled is opt-in for the first release. Related work: follows up on ENG-6012 (subnet ownership tagging) and complements pr-70418 by introducing transient peering and automated cleanup.

review_comments: Marcus Lee: Can you explain how route propagation is gated to avoid transient overlap between old and new control-plane routes?

Anika Patel: We add an explicit propagation sequence: create peering, add routes to secondary RT, validate connectivity, then atomically update DNS. The preflight route conflict detector will block if overlapping routes exist.
Sofia Hargreaves: The security group temporary rules look permissive for the handoff window; can we tighten them to specific control-plane ports only?
Anika Patel: Agreed. Updated SG to only allow TCP 443 and 10250 between control-plane CIDRs for the handoff phase and added expiration tag enforcement.
Diego Alvarez: Integration tests flaked on the first run due to timing; consider adding a jitter and a longer grace period for AWS eventual consistency.
Anika Patel: Added jitter and increased cleanup_grace_seconds with a feature toggle to tune in staging before enabling in prod.
Marcus Lee: Please include a note in release notes about opt-in default and how to enable the feature.
Anika Patel: Included explicit enablement steps in docs/runbooks/controlplane-handoff.md and examples/private/handoff-example.yaml.
release_notes: Opt-in control-plane handoff.workflow: introduces transient peering, secondary control-plane subnet provisioning, DNS TTL tuning, and automated cleanup. Default disabled; see docs/runbooks/controlplane-handoff.md for enablement and rollback steps.
notes_for_ops: Before enabling in customer clusters: 1) run --handoff-dry-run to validate plan and conflicts, 2) reduce DNS TTL to 30s, 3) run canary on one region with monitoring for kubelet heartbeats and API latency. If rollback needed, use installer rollback subcommand which reverses DNS swaps and recreates previous peering.
